stem: Different canopy positions show different flowering response. Which sampling plan is strongest?
choices: Sample the easiest flowers to reach in each zone so the method is practical and repeatable.
Use predefined representative canopy positions and the same observation method across zones and time points.
Use a prior-cycle photo as the main comparison because current positional variation may be temporary.
Average observations across the room without retaining position because room-level flowering is the production outcome.
rationale: When response differs by canopy position, the sampling plan has to preserve position rather than average it away. Predefined representative locations and a consistent observation method make zone-to-zone and time-series comparisons interpretable. Convenience sampling can bias the result toward accessible areas, while historical photos or room averages may miss the spatial pattern that prompted the investigation.
